95201.text: What is the name given to the measures taken to protect the public, passengers, crew, ground personnel, airport buildings and facilities, and air navigation and aviation communication infrastructures against unlawful acts?

95202.text: Which of the following refers to the reduction of risks that directly affect aviation activities or flight operations and keeping them at an acceptable level?

95203.text: Which of the following is the fundamental difference between aviation security and aviation safety?
options: In security occurrences a rule is deliberately violated, whereas in safety occurrences it is a matter of negligence or error rather than intent
Security applies only on the ground, safety applies only in the air
Security protects passengers, while safety protects only the crew
Security is a national concept, while safety is only an international one
Security applies to commercial flights, safety applies to private flights

95204.text: Aviation safety matters are related to the consequences of which of the following situations?
options: Malfunction, manufacturing defect, negligence and forgetfulness

95205.text: Which of the following is NOT among the attack methods used in threats against civil aviation?
options: Aircraft maintenance records being kept incorrectly due to carelessness
Use of the aircraft as a weapon

95206.text: Who are the persons who typically commit individual acts against aviation security?
options: Persons seeking asylum, disgruntled employees or criminals
Only trained members of terrorist organizations

95207.text: Which of the following is the fundamental feature distinguishing organized threats from individual threats?
options: Organizations having extensive resources and conducting systematic work on their actions
Organizations having more limited resources than individuals
Organization members receiving no training whatsoever
Organizations' actions always being predictable in advance
Organizations being able to act only on the ground

95208.text: Although terrorist organizations are formed for various reasons such as political, ideological or religious ones, what is the common goal of all of them?
options: To create fear in society, propagate their own philosophy and gain benefit
To increase the ticket revenues of airline companies
To regulate civil aviation traffic through legal means

95209.text: Which of the following is NOT one of the reasons why civil aviation is an attractive target for terrorists?
options: The possibility of intervention being very wide during attacks in flight
Attracting the attention of world public opinion
Providing an effective means of propaganda
High loss of life and property in attacks during flight

95210.text: What is the name given to persons who are not citizens of the country they are in and who, for any reason, are sent by air to their own country or to another country?
options: Persons in transit for judicial reasons

95211.text: What is the name given to passengers whose entry into a country is refused by the competent authorities due to incomplete documents or an invalid visa?
options: Persons in transit for judicial reasons

95212.text: Under which heading are persons such as suspects, defendants and detainees, who are subject to judicial proceedings and are transferred by air from one place to another, classified?
options: Persons in transit for judicial reasons

95213.text: A passenger who unfastens the seatbelt and stands up before the seatbelt sign is switched off is classified in which group in terms of aviation security?
options: Person in transit for judicial reasons

95214.text: Between 1948 and 1968, acts of unlawful interference against civil aviation were predominantly carried out for which purpose?

95215.text: Between 1968 and 1994, acts of unlawful interference against civil aviation were predominantly carried out for which purpose?

95216.text: From 1994 to the present, acts of unlawful interference have generally been carried out for which purpose?

95217.text: Which of the following is the most frequently used attack tool in acts of unlawful interference?

95218.text: Which of the following is NOT one of the components that make up an explosive device?

95219.text: What is the primary purpose in the analysis of a bomb threat?
options: To assess the credibility of the threat and determine whether it is real
To identify the identity of the attacker
To determine the brand of the explosive
To calculate the commercial loss of the flight

95220.text: By whom and how should the analysis of a bomb threat be carried out?
options: By trained personnel, without wasting time
By any personnel, during working hours
Only by airline company managers, after the flight
By the cabin crew, based on information from passengers
Only upon written request, within a week

95221.text: When are aircraft hijacking acts most often carried out?
options: While the aircraft is parked on the apron
After the landing gear is extended

95222.text: For what purposes did aircraft hijacking incidents originally begin?
options: To seek asylum and commit piracy

95223.text: In the attack that took place at Paris Orly Airport on 27 September 1974, where was the explosive device placed?
options: In a piece of luggage inside a locked locker
In a container in the cargo warehouse
At the entrance of the control tower

95224.text: In the attacks lasting approximately 5 days at London Heathrow Airport starting on 14 March 1994, which weapon was used and what was the outcome?
options: Mortar; there was no serious material damage or injury, and a large number of flights were cancelled
Suicide bomber; 35 people lost their lives
Man-portable air defence system; an aircraft was shot down
Chemical substance; the terminal was evacuated

95225.text: The attack carried out at Domodedovo International Airport in Russia on 24 January 2011 targeted which area, and how many people lost their lives?

95226.text: Which of the following describes the outcome of the attack that took place at Brussels Airport on 22 March 2016?
options: 33 people lost their lives, 250 people were injured, and the airport remained closed for months
2 people were injured, and the airport reopened the same day
35 people lost their lives, 150 people were injured
Only material damage occurred, and flights were cancelled
19 people lost their lives, and the airport closed for a week

95227.text: How many aircraft were used as weapons in the attacks of 11 September 2001?

95228.text: How many people, excluding the hijackers, were reported to have lost their lives in the 11 September 2001 attacks?

95229.text: Where did the fourth aircraft crash in the 11 September 2001 attacks?

95230.text: Which event is regarded as a turning point in terms of aviation security and completely changed the nature of threats?

95231.text: Which of the following is NOT counted among the current threats against civil aviation?
options: The aircraft being delayed due to a technical malfunction

95232.text: Which of the following is NOT true for persons who constitute an insider threat?
options: They are persons from outside the aviation sector who have never entered an airport
They may be members of a terrorist organization
They may assist in attacks in order to obtain a benefit
They may be used by criminal organizations because they do not have adequate security awareness
They are persons working in the aviation sector

95233.text: In which year was the Convention on International Civil Aviation (Chicago Convention) signed?

95234.text: What is the notable feature of the Chicago Convention in terms of aviation security?
options: It contains no direct provision on aviation security
It contains all the implementation details of aviation security
It regulates only the subject of aviation security
It determines the format of airport access cards
It contains the technical standards of security screening

95235.text: In which year was the Tokyo Convention on Offences and Certain Other Acts Committed on Board Aircraft signed?

95236.text: Since the Tokyo Convention was considered not to contain adequate and up-to-date provisions, by which instrument was it replaced?

95237.text: In which year was the Hague Convention for the Suppression of Unlawful Seizure of Aircraft signed?

95238.text: By which instrument was the Hague Convention amended?

95239.text: In which year was the Montreal Convention for the Suppression of Unlawful Acts against the Safety of Civil Aviation signed?

95240.text: Unlike other international conventions, which subjects did the Montreal Protocol adopted in 1988 address?
options: The security of airport employees, facilities and aircraft
Only the marking of plastic explosives

95241.text: In which year was the Convention on the Marking of Plastic Explosives for the Purpose of Detection concluded?

95242.text: Which instruments did the Beijing Convention and the Beijing Protocol replace?
options: The 1971 Montreal Convention and the 1988 Montreal Protocol
The 1944 Chicago Convention and the 1963 Tokyo Convention
The 1970 Hague Convention and the 1991 MEX Convention

95243.text: How many Annexes have been published in addition to the main text of the Convention on International Civil Aviation?

95244.text: In which year was Annex 17, titled "Security: Safeguarding International Civil Aviation Against Acts of Unlawful Interference", adopted?

95245.text: In which Annex is the structure of the reinforced cockpit door for the protection of the aircraft cockpit specified?

95246.text: In which Annex are the headings for inadmissible passengers and the control of travel documents regulated?

95247.text: Which of the following is ICAO Document 8973?

95248.text: Which of the following is true regarding the content of ICAO Document 8973?
options: It contains detailed explanations of the general principles set out in Annex 17, together with the implementation procedures of the standards and recommended practices
It contains only a list of convention texts
It is an abridged summary of Annex 17
It contains only examples of national legislation

95249.text: Which elements do the quality control activities under the National Aviation Security Quality Control Programme cover?

95250.text: What is the purpose of the National Aviation Security Quality Control Programme?
options: To determine the level of compliance of the applied legislation and security measures with the national civil aviation security programme
To determine the salaries of airport personnel

95251.text: Which of the following must be determined through the National Civil Aviation Security Training Programme?
options: The certification requirements for screening personnel and instructors
The colour of airport access cards
The rest periods of the flight crew

95252.text: Which of the following is true regarding the Airport Security Programme?
options: It is drawn up for each airport in a manner consistent with the national programme and containing features specific to that airport
It is prepared as a single, common text for all airports
It is prepared only for airports operating international flights
It is not required to be in writing
It is drawn up only in times of crisis

95253.text: In Türkiye, with which document and in which year was the requirement for a National Civil Aviation Security Programme met?
options: National Civil Aviation Quality Control Programme - 1986

95254.text: Which of the following is true regarding national aviation security legislation?
options: Merely accepting international standards and rules is not sufficient; they must be transposed into the domestic legal and legislative system
Accepting international standards is sufficient on its own
National legislation is prepared independently of international legislation
National needs do not need to be taken into account
Regulation needs to be made only at a single level

95255.text: By which body are ICAO's aviation security standards prepared?

95256.text: After which stages do ICAO aviation security standards enter into force?
options: After the approval of the Council, ICAO's executive body, and the approval of member States
Only by the approval of member States
By a simple majority of the Assembly
By the approval of airport security committees

95257.text: According to Annex 17, which structures must the national organization include at a minimum?
options: The appropriate authority, the national civil aviation security committee, the local authority and the airport security committee
Only the appropriate authority and the airport security committee
The appropriate authority, the quality control unit and the training unit
Only the national committee and the local authority
The appropriate authority, the airline operator and the air traffic service provider

95258.text: According to Annex 17, which of the following is true regarding the appropriate authority appointed by a member State?
options: The appointed authority must be notified to ICAO
It can only be the civil aviation authority; it cannot be another institution
It does not need to be notified to ICAO
It is appointed separately for each airport
It operates only during periods of crisis

95259.text: Which institution has been designated as the civil aviation security authority in Türkiye and notified to ICAO?

95260.text: In Türkiye, which structure was established to carry out the duties of the National Civil Aviation Security Committee?
options: The Central Security Board, established by Regulation No. 9707

95261.text: In Türkiye, which structure was established to carry out secretariat services, prepare technical opinions, and conduct airport-level quality control activities in support of the airport security authority's duties?
options: Board of Training, Research and Inspection Experts

95262.text: Which of the following is the airport security authority empowered to do?
options: To take and implement the necessary measures, and to inspect the operations of organizations
To approve the aircraft maintenance programme

95263.text: According to the responsibilities of the Airport Security Committee, how should security surveys and inspections be carried out?
options: Once a year, announced in advance
Only upon the request of the appropriate authority

95264.text: Which of the following is one of the responsibilities of the Airport Security Committee?
options: Identifying vulnerable areas, including essential equipment and facilities, and regularly reviewing their security
Drafting and publishing the national programme

95265.text: In terms of aviation security, into which sections are airports divided?
options: Landside, airside and security restricted areas
Domestic flights, international flights and cargo
Departing passengers, arriving passengers and transit
Civilian zone, military zone and free zone
